newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Pressures may increase in 1997, Firestone cautions.
newsitem.headline: Pressures may increase in 1997, Firestone cautions.

text.p: Tyre manufacturer Firestone New Zealand Ltd on Wednesday cautioned that the pressures of the strong currency and competition from low priced imported tyres were unlikely to lessen in 1997, and if anything they would increase.
Earlier, the company reported a full year profit of NZ$4.24 million against $7.18 million last year. A dividend of 10 cents per share was declared.
Firestone said it was a poor finish to the year after a strong start, with the company battling the strong New Zealand dollar and cut-price competition.
The profit decrease of 41 percent on the 1995 figure was on slightly lower turnover of NZ$120.8 million compared to $122.4 million in 1995.
Chairman and managing director John Jenkins said Firestone's answer to the tougher trading conditions was renewed efforts to cut costs and lift productivity.
He said the new tyre plant has made progress in 1996, reducing manufacturing costs through improved productivity and Kaizen activities.
After overcoming problems at the start of the year, production levels went on to reach new highs and establish new standards for tyre production in the second half.
The company said that new capital would be spent in 1997 in areas where significant savings could be achieved in waste and scrap reduction, and maximising mould and curing capacity.
